props.title: Grease
props.initialSlug: Summer love blossoms in 1950s high school musical

sections.content: Grease (1978) revolutionized the movie musical with its irresistible blend of 1950s nostalgia and late 1970s energy. John Travolta and Olivia Newton-John's electric chemistry as Danny and Sandy created the template for countless teen romances. The film builds on earlier rock musicals like American Graffiti (1973) but adds a glossier, more accessible style that influenced later hits like Footloose (1984) and Dirty Dancing (1987). The soundtrack dominated Billboard charts, with "You're the One That I Want" and "Summer Nights" becoming cultural touchstones that transcended the film itself.

sections.content: The success of Grease sparked a wave of retro musicals and teen films. Fame (1980) brought gritty realism to the genre while maintaining high-energy musical numbers. Little Shop of Horrors (1986) merged 1960s nostalgia with campy horror. Director Randal Kleiser's decision to cast established pop star Olivia Newton-John set a precedent for musicians crossing over into film musicals, paving the way for Purple Rain (1984) with Prince and Crossroads (2002) with Britney Spears. SUBHEAD: The Teen Musical Revolution

Grease fundamentally changed how Hollywood approached teen-focused musicals. Its influence echoes through High School Musical (2006), which similarly combines contemporary style with classic musical theater tropes. The film's memorable ensemble numbers inspired the structured group performances in Pitch Perfect (2012) and Glee (2009-2015). Even non-musical teen films like 10 Things I Hate About You (1999) borrowed from Grease's blueprint of transformative romance and high school social dynamics.
